sources.title: Service Agreement
sources.text:
SERVICE AGREEMENT (fictional)

4. Duties
4.1 The Executive shall devote the whole of their working time to the business of the Company.

12. Restrictions
12.2 For six months after the Termination Date the Executive shall not solicit any Client.

18. Garden leave
18.1 The Company may place the Executive on garden leave for up to three months.

citing.title: Advice on the executive's exit
citing.text:
ADVICE ON THE EXECUTIVE'S EXIT (fictional)

1. Restrictions
1.1 Clause 12.2 of the Service Agreement says that "For twelve months after the Termination Date the Executive shall not solicit any Client."
1.2 Clause 18.1 of the Service Agreement allows garden leave "for up to three months".
1.3 Clause 22.5 of the Service Agreement is said to cover expenses.

2. Law
2.1 The Executive may claim under section 98 of the Employment Rights Act 1996, and the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999 does not apply.
2.2 On restraint of trade see [2019] UKSC 32 and Herbert Morris Ltd v Saxelby [1916] 1 AC 688.
2.3 The Company's reliance on [2003] UKSC 14 is misplaced.

MEMORANDUM ON THE DISTRIBUTION NETWORK (fictional)

1. Framework

2. Analysis
2.1 As explained in paragraph 1.1, the block exemption may apply. Paragraph 3.4 sets out the market shares.

sources.title: Master Services Agreement
sources.text:
MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT (fictional)

Section 5. Fees
5.2 Customer shall pay all undisputed invoices within forty-five (45) days of receipt.

Section 9. Limitation of Liability
9.1 In no event shall either party's aggregate liability exceed the fees paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim.

Section 13. Term
13.1 This Agreement shall continue for an initial term of three (3) years.

citing.title: Memorandum on the MSA
citing.text:
MEMORANDUM ON THE MSA (fictional)

1. Payment
1.1 Section 5.2 of the Master Services Agreement requires payment "within forty-five (45) days of receipt."
1.2 Section 9.1 of the Master Services Agreement provides that "In no event shall either party's aggregate liability exceed the fees paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim."
1.3 Under Section 13.1 of the Master Services Agreement, the initial term is three years.

2. Authorities
2.1 See 9 U.S.C. § 2; 29 C.F.R. Part 1630; Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(1); and Harlow Systems, Inc. v. Brandt, 245 A.3d 101 (Del. Ch. 2021).
2.2 The plaintiff relies on 54 U.S.C. § 100101, but 63 U.S.C. § 12 does not exist.
